title: Finite-type closed subspaces of affine limits are eventually closed
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback along every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. An affine morphism is representable by schemes and has affine scheme source after every affine scheme test. Local finite type and local finite presentation are tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation. A closed immersion is a representable morphism that is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $B$ be an algebraic space, $I$ a small nonempty directed set, and $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of algebraic spaces over $B$ with affine transition morphisms. Suppose each $X_i$ is quasi-compact and the fppf sheaf limit $X=\varprojlim_i X_i$ is an algebraic space. Let $h:T\to X$ be a closed immersion over $B$ and assume $T\to B$ locally of finite type. Then there exists $i_1\in I$ such that $T\to X_i$ is a closed immersion for every $i\ge i_1$.

proof.text: Fix $o\in I$. By [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement], choose an affine scheme $C$ with a representable surjective etale map $C\to X_o$. Apply [lem-a1-qc-map-affine-etale-neighbourhood] to the quasi-compact scheme $C$ and its composite $C\to B$. Obtain an affine scheme $W$ with a representable etale map $W\to B$ such that $P=C\times_BW\to C$ is surjective etale. Put $E=X_o\times_BW$. The scheme $P$ exists by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]; its map to $E$ is the base change of $C\to X_o$, hence representable surjective etale. Its composite $P\to C\to X_o$ is also representable surjective etale. No quasi-compactness of $P$ or $E$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0828 (lemma-finite-type-eventually-closed), proof (1), choice of W; omitted atlas details via spaces-properties.tex Tags 03H6 and 0APL (proposition-sheaf-fpqc), affine-chart paragraph

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement] to the specified scheme atlas $P\to X_o$, using quasi-compactness of $X_o$. It supplies an affine scheme $U_o$, a map $U_o\to P$, and a representable surjective etale composite $U_o\to X_o$. The compatible scheme map $U_o\to P$ is etale by the final clause of [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], since both maps to $X_o$ are representable etale. Composing it with $P\to E$ shows that $U_o\to X_o\times_BW$ is representable etale. This proves exactly the adapted atlas assertion omitted in the source, without requiring $B$ quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 0828, proof (1): choose U_0 and the parenthetical details omitted; spaces-properties.tex Tags 03E4 and 03H6, refinement of a specified atlas

proof.text: For $i\ge o$ set $U_i=X_i\times_{X_o}U_o$ and $U=X\times_{X_o}U_o$. The transition maps and the projection $X\to X_o$ are affine by [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages]. Thus all $U_i$ and $U$ are affine schemes, and the transitions $U_j\to U_i$ are affine, by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality]. The maps $U_i\to X_i$ and $U\to X$ are representable surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. The base-change clause of [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages] identifies $U$ with the inverse limit of the $U_i$ as fppf sheaves. This is also their scheme limit: a morphism of schemes into these represented sheaves is precisely a scheme morphism, by [def-trf-algebraic-space], so their limiting Hom-bijection restricts to scheme tests. Only the unconditional affine-projection and base-change clauses are used; the eventual-schematicity clause requiring quasi-separated stages is not used.

source.place: Tag 0828, proof (1), definition of the pulled-back system; Tag 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), clauses (1),(2)

proof.text: Put $V=T\times_XU=T\times_{X_o}U_o$. Since $h:T\to X$ is representable closed, $V\to U$ is a closed immersion of schemes. The affine closed-immersion criterion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] makes $V$ affine. The map $V\to T\times_BW$ is the base change of $U_o\to X_o\times_BW$ along $T\times_BW\to X_o\times_BW$, so is representable etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Since $T\to B$ is locally of finite type, its compatible etale chart $V\to W$ is locally of finite type, using exactly the chart test stipulated in the statement. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] says that $D=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ is a finitely generated $R=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$-algebra.

source.place: Tag 0828, proof (1), reduction to V over W; limits.tex Tag 081B (lemma-finite-type-eventually-closed), proof (1), affine reduction; morphisms.tex Tag 01T2

proof.text: Write $A_i=\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_{U_i})$ and $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. Each $U_i$ has the compatible map to $W$ inherited from $U_o$, so these are compatible $R$-algebras. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], applied to the affine scheme system from step 3, $A=\varinjlim_{i\ge o}A_i$. All maps to $V$ are induced by the original $B$-morphism $T\to X$: explicitly $V\to U_i$ sends a pair $(t,u_o)$ to $(h_i(t),u_o)$, where $h_i:T\to X_i$ is its composite. Thus the ring maps $q_i:A_i\to D$ and $q:A\to D$ commute with transitions and the $R$-maps. The map $q$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] applied to $V\hookrightarrow U$.

source.place: Tag 081B, proof (1), the displayed algebra fact; Tag 01YW (lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit)

proof.text: Choose finitely many $R$-algebra generators $d_1,\ldots,d_r$ of $D$ and lifts $a_1,\ldots,a_r\in A$ through the surjection $q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-global-sections-colimit] every $a_k$ is the image of a section at some stage; its hypotheses hold because the $U_i$ are affine schemes and the transitions affine. A common upper bound $i_1\ge o$ for these finitely many stages provides elements of $A_{i_1}$ mapping to all $d_k$. For every $i\ge i_1$, their transition images still map to the $d_k$, while the image of $q_i$ contains the structural image of $R$. Every element of $D$ is a polynomial in the $d_k$ with coefficients in $R$, so $q_i$ is surjective. If $r=0$, take $i_1=o$: the image of $R$ already generates $D$.

source.place: Tag 081B, proof (1), finite-generator argument for the displayed algebra fact; Tag 01Z0 (lemma-descend-section), representatives

proof.text: For every $i\ge i_1$, the affine schemes $V$ and $U_i$ and the surjection $q_i:A_i\to D$ satisfy the singleton affine-cover criterion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion]. Hence $V\to U_i$ is a closed immersion. Its square with $T\to X_i$ is cartesian: $T\times_{X_i}U_i=T\times_{X_i}(X_i\times_{X_o}U_o)=T\times_{X_o}U_o=V$, with the map to $U_i$ exactly $(t,u_o)\mapsto(h_i(t),u_o)$ from step 5.

source.place: Tag 0828, proof (1), V to U_i and the cartesian base-change identification

proof.text: For each $i\ge i_1$, $U_i\to X_i$ is the representable surjective etale cover from step 3. It is flat and locally of finite presentation on compatible etale scheme charts: [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests] makes those scheme chart maps etale, and [def-weil-etale-morphism] includes flatness and local finite presentation. The singleton cover therefore satisfies all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-fppf-descent]. Its pullback of $T\to X_i$ is the closed immersion $V\to U_i$ from step 7, so that node proves that $T\to X_i$ is a representable closed immersion. This holds for every $i\ge i_1$, as claimed.
